For the Outline §6b: (1) Target-recalibrated regression (§3b) does not beat the plain mean on the same design (strat × recal 1.03 [1.02,1.05] of strat × mean in extrapolation; balanced × recal-s 0.97 vs balanced × mean 0.95; fall-back 0.4–1.3% extrap, 21–22% interp/lineage at n=100, mostly the fallback at 2% of N on high-accuracy small-n benchmarks). Say so; it is the post-results estimator and a negative result, not a method. (2) §3c was not run: 'not run', future work. (3) The weak-prior check (prior variance ×10) cuts the IRT model's extrapolation squared bias by ~29% (4.29 → 3.04 of uniform × mean's MSE) and its RMSE ratio 1.96 → 1.66; the model-based predictor stays worse than uniform above the sources, so the prior is not the cause (an after-the-fact check, label it). (4) Suggested reading that follows from the ceiling analysis: the sources buy a limited variance reduction that can be taken through the design or through the estimator, mostly not both; the extra gain in extrapolation sits in the balanced × (calibrated or difference) pairing; estimator correction is for robustness. Headline wording remains yours; the extrapolation hold I asked for in idea-repo#4 is lifted. Numbers are analysis's (experiment-repo#6 comment); check against its results/ before use.
